newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen opening lower as correction continues.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen opening lower as correction continues.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open lower on Friday, continuing the two-day sell-off that has seen the Dow tumble nearly 170 points.
For now, analysts are generally viewing the sharp and sudden reversal of fortune for blue chips as a correction from their powerful November rally.
"The market's in a corrective stage and I think we have another 100 points before we see some stabilization," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Analysts noted that the hardest hit stocks so far have largely been the same ones that posted the strongest rally last month, those in the Dow.

"When we talk about working off excesses on the upside, we're really talking about a Dow advance and a Dow decline," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. In contrast, he noted, the Russell 2000 index of small-cap stocks registered a relatively small loss yesterday.
Analysts also said at least some of the recent reflected a race between money managers to lock in profits for the year.
"You can certainly understand a money manager deciding to pack it in at this point and saying why risk getting into trouble for the last three weeks of the year," Wachtel said.

In Tokyo, stocks finished lower, but managed to bounce back from steep declines early in the session. The Nikkei-225 index plunged nearly 550 points before recovering to close at 20,341, for a 160 point loss.
U.S. stocks were modestly weaker in London. The FTSe-100 fell 45 points to 3946.
The dollar firmed in Tokyo but retraced some gains in Europe to stand at 113 yen and just below 1.54 marks.
U.S. Treasuries were little changed. The 30-year bond eased 2/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
The March S&P 500 index future fell 5.25 to 729.25.
Data due today include October business inventories and the University of Michigan's preliminary December consumer sentiment survey, both due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
The New York Times Marketplace column reports on a plan to post key documents related to securities class action suits on the Internet.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports Quaker Oats Co is shopping its Snapple unit.

The column said investment bankers confirmed Quaker Oats is seeking a buyer for the business, although Quaker declined to comment. Quaker has previously declined comment on rumors it was seeking such a sale.
